hints: Focus on the two different trends separately, radius goes down a group while conductivity is about metals across a period.
List each element with its group and period, for Group 2 the order from top is Be then Mg then Ca.
In Period 3 the three metals conduct best in the order Al then Mg then Na, so look for the element that is second in both of its lists.
walkthrough:
**Recall the group trend for atomic radius**

Atomic radius increases down a group because each new period adds another electron shell. So the top element is smallest, the next one down is second smallest.

Trend down a group:
$$\text{atomic radius increases down the group}$$

**Recall the period trend for electrical conductivity**

Electrical conductivity is highest for metals with delocalised electrons and falls sharply to non-metals. In Period 3, $\text{Na}$, $\text{Mg}$ and $\text{Al}$ are the metals, and conductivity increases with charge and electron density, so $\text{Al} > \text{Mg} > \text{Na}$.

**Test the Group 2 elements**

Group 2 order from the top is $\text{Be} > \text{Mg} > \text{Ca} > \text{Sr} > \text{Ba}$ in size. That makes $\text{Be}$ the smallest and $\text{Mg}$ the second smallest, while $\text{Ca}$ is third.

**Combine both clues to decide**

$\text{Mg}$ is second smallest in Group 2 and also second best conductor in Period 3 behind $\text{Al}$. No other listed element is second in both its own group and its own period.

options.A: Boron is in Group 13 and Period 2. In Group 13, boron is at the top so it is the smallest, not the second smallest. In Period 2 it is a metalloid with much lower conductivity than lithium and beryllium.
options.B: Calcium is in Group 2 and Period 4. In Group 2 the size order is Be (smallest), Mg (second), Ca (third), so calcium is too large. In Period 4 it is also not the second best conductor because potassium and transition metals like copper conduct better.
options.C: Magnesium is in Group 2 and Period 3. Down Group 2, Be is smallest and Mg is next, so second smallest. Across Period 3, Al conducts best, Mg is next, and Na is third, so Mg is second highest for conductivity. It fits both conditions.
options.D: Sodium is in Group 1 and Period 3. It is indeed second smallest in Group 1 (Li is smallest), so it passes the first test. However in Period 3 conductivity follows Al > Mg > Na, so sodium is third, not second. This is the classic trap of meeting only one condition.
